notes: No criterion scored below 5; nothing was absent, wrong, or asserted without the reasoning the rubric demands. Observed gate: keys on gh repo view per remote with the host carried, records manifest agreement and separately works the posture axis with the right rule ('fully-private is a mismatch only over an observed-public repo'), so the agreement is reasoned rather than assumed. Repo set: built from every root-carrying manifest object (two), each with a block and the §2 row that governs it; the ai_workspace gate states why the role row beats the `any` row and what an undeterminable read on an on-record remote would have cost, showing the arm was derived not guessed. No silent narrowing: policy-file shape checked (not 120000/160000), rule block integrity checked, full-clone facts cited for scan completeness, and 'Degradations: None' is justified item by item rather than manufactured on an all-inputs-present scenario. Semantic pass: named skip on both arms with the observed value, and explicitly does not descend because the arm does not run it; no S1/S2 invented and the single moat row was not used as a comparison set. Scan-first: sweep is a named skip, and the report refuses to launder the scenario's 'no untracked files' into a classification this run produced, and refuses to descend into the submodule for §4 because the arm runs no sweep at all (arm-scoped skip, correctly distinguished from the uninitialized-submodule INCONCLUSIVE). Disposition: §6-skipping arms, so the two hygiene notes are recorded and reach the user without being dispositioned; no override, no inventory row, allowlist untouched. Verdict shape: one verdict, six checks accounted per block, every skip carrying its observed value, submodule pin commit named in the block, standing warnings recapped as empty, and the not-shipped dimensions named by class so clean does not overstate coverage. History pass: correctly named-skipped on both repos off the exposure (every remote on record reads private), with the inventory's missing History passes table explicitly not a finding, and the scan never read as covering the document rules or §5. Tree pinning: canonical ref resolved from the spines' base_branch with default_branch as cross-check, HEAD proved by comparing two resolved object ids, ls-files -v checked so the quiet diffs count as evidence, and on the secrets-scan-only arm the clean tree is correctly ran-clean off the two diff checks with no scan claimed as owed. Submodule descent: the descent rides the canonical's arm (§3 rules + §3 secrets read at the pin, §4 and §5 not descending because the arm skips them), policy is the superproject's boundary file matched under both anchorings with the finding named superproject-relative, the submodule's own missing boundary file correctly not a finding, fixtures-must-be asked of the pinned tree, history not descending while the working-tree pass does, the pin established by the submodule's OWN two quiet diffs plus the absence of index flags with the submodule.<name>.ignore reason given, and the operator's 'not our repository to audit' refused on the ground that the pin is what the canonical publishes.
